title: Spirit Circle
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fuuta Okeya, a middle schooler who can see ghosts, meets transfer student Kouko Ishigami, who recognizes him as her enemy from past lives and attacks him with a flaming spirit circle. Using the circle, Fuuta relives a chain of past incarnations across eras in which he and Kouko wronged and killed each other. He tries to understand those lives and break the cycle of revenge.
life_message: Grudges carried across lifetimes only end through understanding and forgiveness, and life is worth living because something good will happen.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kouko's honor-driven vengeance is what Fuuta works to dissolve; forgiveness replaces retaliation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Past lives show both oppressive orders (village sacrifice) and personal choice.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Fuuta cares for strangers and enemies, not just family; found families recur.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Priestess overruled by village authority; story sides with the dissenter.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Rebirth and spirits are real; meaning comes from a spiritual frame.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Ends on hope and finding beauty in life despite suffering.

folkways.japan: Lingering grudges (onnen) across lives and the ghost companion draw on Japanese Buddhist-folk ideas of karma and restless spirits.

delivery.evidence: A Wrong Every Time essay says the forgiveness theme is built through character arcs and treats Kouko's revenge as understandable but self-defeating.
delivery.note: Its message of forgiveness is carried by past-life stories and character arcs, with the case for revenge given real weight.

winners_losers: Fuuta's forgiveness wins and Kouko's hatred softens; the logic of revenge loses. Sympathy goes to compassion.
